prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its active form, which underlie incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: I keep a single-part B045 prize to Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The round-1 exchange did not weaken the scientific case: the chain from incretin physiology (Holst) and proglucagon processing and receptor biology (Drucker) to the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide (Mojsov) is original, mechanistically clear and independently confirmed in large outcome trials for glycaemia, weight, and cardiovascular and renal disease. It is mature without being late, and it is a physiology discovery in the sense the prize intends. All six of us landed on the same three names, but I do not treat that as an argument; what persuades me is that no one has offered a stronger discovery-credit combination. A single part also avoids the arbitrary exclusions that any two-part configuration would force under the three-person cap, since B045 would have to shrink to two names to make room for a second part.
statement.case_against: Attribution remains the weak point, and round 1 did not resolve it. Mojsov's priority for the active peptide form is contested and Habener, who is outside the credited names, is part of that dispute; I cannot settle it from the supplied materials and I have not verified primary sources. Knudsen's acylated analogues are what made liraglutide and semaglutide practical drugs, and the committee should be honest that leaving her out is a judgement about what the prize rewards, not something the science decides. A prize that names the physiology but not the drug designer can be read as stopping short of the therapy. I think that cost is acceptable, but it is a real cost.

responses.point: Sandberg agrees with the trio but says the cap makes the Mojsov-Habener question harder than the opening arguments admitted, and that we should check the record on who first identified and synthesised the active peptide and not assume her priority.
responses.response: I accept the correction to my own round-1 position, where I asked for a primary-literature check without saying what I would do with the result. Having reread the exchange, the supplied materials give us no way to rank Mojsov's claim against Habener's, so I will not pretend the check has been done. My decision rule is this: Mojsov's credit rests on the identification and synthesis of the active truncated peptide, a distinct scientific step that the pharmacology depended on, and a contested priority does not erase it. If the committee's own review before the final ballot concluded that her claim was clearly secondary, I would reopen the third seat. Absent that, I keep her.

responses.point: El-Manira opened with Knudsen but now says the Drucker, Holst and Mojsov trio is the better fit, while insisting that excluding Knudsen has a cost and that the citation should name the therapeutic outcome.
responses.response: I am glad we have converged on the names, and I agree with you that her exclusion should be stated openly, not treated as costless. I disagree slightly on how the citation should carry it. Naming incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity acknowledges the therapeutic result without crediting any individual who is not a laureate, and I would keep the wording on the discovery side, with the drugs as consequence. I also take your point that her acylation strategy was a real mechanistic idea and not routine engineering; that is why I regard this as a close judgement on what the prize is for, and why I would revisit it if Mojsov's priority were judged unsupportable.

responses.point: Perlmann disagrees that CAR-T should sit directly behind GLP-1, noting that Eshhar's chimeric receptor concept is outside the credited names and that Rosenberg's adoptive-transfer line is a related but different achievement.
responses.response: You are right, and your argument moves me. I ranked CAR-T second on clinical proof and its status as a new class of living therapeutic, but I did not weigh enough that a trio of June, Sadelain and Rosenberg blends two stories while leaving out the originator of the chimeric receptor concept. I have therefore dropped B025 as an alternative. I would still regard it as a serious candidate for a later year once the attribution has been thought through, but it is not a credible fallback this year.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius says that if Mojsov's claim were judged unresolvable, a Holst and Drucker pair would be a better fallback than swapping in a developer, and that B003 is her lead if B045 stalls on credit allocation.
responses.response: I agree that a two-name B045 is a better fallback than substituting Knudsen, since it keeps the prize on discovery and does not require the committee to resolve the dispute by default. I would add that it would be a worse outcome than the trio only if Mojsov's contribution is judged real, so I would want that question put directly to the committee. On B003, I agree with you and with Per that the zur Hausen prize covers the viral aetiology and not VLP vaccine design, so novelty is not the bar. I raised my own ranking of it for this round, and it is my first fallback because the Lowy and Schiller L1 VLP work gives it a secure core.

responses.point: The chair asks whether the committee rewards GLP-1 discovery alone or also the translation, and how the citation should be worded so Knudsen's role is acknowledged if she is not a laureate; he also treats B003 as the principal alternative and B015 as a strong one.
responses.response: My answer to the chair's question is discovery first, with the translation acknowledged through the citation, not through a fourth person. On the fallbacks, I now align with you on B003 first and B015 second. B015 has a clean two-person credit to Walter and Mori and a conceptually elegant mechanism, and I ranked it seventh in the opening mainly because its disease link is still developing. That is a timing argument and not a doubt about the science, and for a fallback it matters less than a clean attribution does.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1 peptide is secure enough, relative to Habener, to hold the third seat; I have not verified this against primary sources and the supplied materials do not settle it.
Whether the committee prefers to reward discovery alone or discovery together with the translation to drugs, and whether the citation can carry Knudsen's role without implying a fourth laureate.
Whether B003 or B015 is the better fallback, given the Zhou and parallel VLP-group questions for B003 and the still-developing disease relevance for B015.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent for any shortlisted ballot. I have co-authored with Rickard Sandberg and others, including the 2016 Science spatial transcriptomics paper, and I am at Karolinska Institutet, but none of the credited names on B045, B003, B015 or the other shortlisted ballots is a documented collaborator, so I see no basis for recusal. This updates my round-1 note only in that I have now read the other members' disclosures, and none changes it.
